entities.paper: Reverse-Engineering Satire, or"Paper on Computational Humor Accepted Despite Making Serious Advances"

onion_satirical_corpus.text: 是的，论文使用 The Onion 作为数据集的一部分：其讽刺新闻标题语料由 The Onion 发布的 9,159 条标题组成。

serious_corpus.text: 与讽刺语料配对的是严肃新闻语料，共 9,000 条标题，取自 9 个主要新闻网站。

onion_corpus_use.text: 作者对 The Onion 语料中全部 9,159 条原始标题进行了切块分析。

onion_example.text: 论文以 The Onion 发表的讽刺标题“God diagnosed with bipolar disorder”作为贯穿示例。

onion_corpus_size.text: The paper's satirical corpus consists of 9,159 headlines published by The Onion.

serious_corpus_size.text: The serious corpus used alongside the satirical corpus consists of 9,000 headlines drawn from 9 major news websites.

acceptance_rate_humor_creation.text: According to the paper, at The Onion only 16 of 600 headlines generated each week (less than 3%) are accepted, which the authors cite as evidence that creating satirical headlines requires a level of creative talent few people have.

reverse_crowdsourcing_rationale.text: The authors observe that removing humor from a satirical headline via small edits is typically straightforward, and that this reverse direction requires much less creativity than crafting the humorous headline in the first place.

dataset_form.text: The dataset presented is a corpus of aligned pairs of satirical and similar-but-serious-looking headlines, rather than individual texts, collected via the online game Unfun.me.

data_release.text: The data collected via Unfun.me, as well as the code for analyzing it, is made publicly available online.

purpose_fine_granularity.text: The aligned-pair corpus is intended to enable analyzing the humor-carrying words that make the difference between serious and funny, at a finer granularity than prior work that compared average satirical headlines to average serious ones.

script_opposition.text: The paper states that the script opposition invalidating the logical step from P(x) to H(x) must be along dimensions contrasting 'good' vs. 'bad', and that satirical headlines differ from typical jokes in tending to make the 'bad' side explicit.

false_analogy_template.text: The paper reports that a large fraction of all headlines from The Onion—and an overwhelming fraction of those in single-substitution pairs—can be analyzed with the false-analogy template.

multiple_substitutions_same_opposition.text: The paper states that whenever multiple substitutions are applied, they all need to follow the same opposition.

double_rating_task.text: The game generates a type-1 task with probability 1/3 and a type-2 task with probability 2/3, such that two ratings per modified headline can be collected; ratings from task 2 serve as a filter whose precision can be increased by decreasing alpha.

theory_basis.text: The authors state that the most widely accepted theory of verbal humor is the General Theory of Verbal Humor by Attardo and Raskin, an extension of Raskin's Semantic-Script Theory of Humor, which they summarize when discussing their findings.
